items.body: Forwards had been sidelined since early October with knee injuries Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand returned for the Florida Panthers against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena on Wednesday. Each forward participated in an optional morning skate and were all smiles afterwards. Barkov was the center on the first line between Carter Verhaeghe and Sam Reinhart . Marchand skated at right wing on the third line with left wing Eetu Luostarinen and center Sam Bennett . "They're both in so we're pretty excited," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. Barkov, who is Florida's captain, injured his left knee Oct. 1, his second game of the season, a 4-3 overtime loss at the San Jose Sharks. items.body: Register Login Ducks Recall Laurent Brossoit By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 6:00 pm The Anaheim Ducks will have their oldest netminder back in the starters’ crease this evening. According to a team announcement , the Ducks recalled goaltender Laurent Brossoit from the San Diego Gulls in the AHL, and he will start tonight against the San Jose Sharks. Technically, tonight’s contest will be Brossoit’s first against his former team. Still, he didn’t have a lengthy history with the Sharks organization. In 2024, the Chicago Blackhawks signed Brossoit to a two-year, $6.6MM contract in free agency. Unfortunately, hip and knee injuries prevented him from playing a game with the Blackhawks. Chicago traded Brossoit to San Jose last January. By the time his contract ended, Brossoit had appeared in only one game with the Sharks. Regardless, he landed on his feet this past summer, inking a one-year, $1MM deal with the Ducks as their third-string netminder. On Halloween, after Anaheim had lost seven of their last eight contests, they recalled Brossoit to debut with the club. Although his save percentage (.867 SV%) and goals-against average (3.42) weren’t good, Anaheim won four of Brossoit’s five appearances, effectively turning their season around. Unfortunately, since Brossoit’s last start on November 11th, the Ducks are in a similar situation. They’ve lost five of their six matchups since Brossoit was reassigned. Even though his numbers weren’t great, Anaheim may now be playing into superstition and will lean on Brossoit if they win.

items.title: Could Montreal's Trade For Dylan Larkin Set Up An All-Canadian Stanley Cup Final?
items.summary: It's been over three decades since a Canadian NHL team won the Stanley Cup. Not only could we get a Canadian champion this season, we could be headed for the first all-Canadian Final since 1989.
items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Adam Proteau Partner Nov 25, 2026 10:19 PM Published Nov 25, 2026 10:19 PM It's been over three decades since a Canadian NHL team won the Stanley Cup. Not only could we get a Canadian champion this season, we could be headed for the first all-Canadian Final since 1989. Every NHL season carries one question that fans seemingly can't get enough of: When will the next Canadian team win the Stanley Cup? Some years, a slew of Canadian teams at least have the opportunity and roster makeup to go on a lengthy playoff run. Other years, you can really only argue that one or two Canadian teams at most have a legitimate shot at winning a Cup. But after Sunday night's blockbuster trade that sent star center Dylan Larkin from the Detroit Red Wings to the Montreal Canadiens , the idea of a Canadian Cup-winner is not only a distinct possibility – but a case can be made for an all-Canadian Cup final between Montreal and the Edmonton Oilers . It would be the first all-Canadian final since the Habs and Calgary Flames went head-to-head at the conclusion of the 1988-89 season. The Oilers lead the Pacific division and are just three points behind the Minnesota Wild as the second-best team in the West. They're in the midst of a four-game losing skid, but the Oilers' big guns have looked like they're on a mission, and the areas of goaltending and defense that have hindered them in previous years have quickly become stronger. Meanwhile, the Canadiens are coming off an appearance in the Eastern Conference Final and sit tied for second in the Atlantic with a 14-7-4 record. They’ve gone 2-10-1 since Marchenko’s absence, caused by an awkward leg twist. “I just go for, like, a goalie butterfly. Need to work more on that next time to not be injured,” Marchenko said. “It’s frustrating, for sure. It’s personally been a long month, but now it's finished already. I'm happy for that. items.title: Sea Lions sign Reichen Kirchmair to one-year contract
items.summary: Kirchmair was taken by the expansion franchise in the sixth round of the 2026 PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL Another young prospect is heading to the Bay Area, inking her first professional contract. On Wednesday, the San Jose Sea Lions signed forward Reichen Kirchmaier to a one-year contract for the 2026-27 season. Kirchmair was taken by the Sea Lions in the sixth round, 64th overall, of the 2026 PWHL draft . She was the expansion franchise’s sixth and final selection in Detroit this past June, adding to a solid core of young players that includes Laila Edwards, Sloane Matthews and Tia Chan. Kirchmair had an impressive NCAA career at Providence College. Over four seasons with the Friars, the Oakville, Ontario native registered an even 100 points, scoring 55 goals and 42 assists across 142 career games. In her senior season, Kirchmair led Providence in goals (14) and points (25), as the team captain was just one of two players on the roster to reach double digits in goals. She led all of Hockey East in scoring during her junior year, earning player of the year honors after scoring 19 goals and 37 points in 35 games. The 22-year-old also became the 29th player in Providence College Women’s Hockey history to reach the century mark in points. Kirchmair also has some international experience. Back in 2022, she represented Canada at the IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship, playing alongside fellow Sea Lions draft pick Mckenna Van Gelder. The duo helped the Canadians take home the gold medal, knocking off the United States. With the signing, the Sea Lions now have 21 players signed to standard player agreements for their inaugural season. items.body: Register Login Parker Wotherspoon Has A Lot Riding On This Season By Josh Cybulski | at November 25, 2026 3:52 pm Vegas Golden Knights defenseman Parker Wotherspoon recently returned from injury and recorded his first point of the season. The injury kept him out of the lineup for 13 games, which hasn’t been ideal given what he and the Golden Knights hope to accomplish this season. Wotherspoon was happy to get the point, but just one assist in 12 games is a steep drop from last season, when he scored 30 points in 80 games with the Pittsburgh Penguins. A lot of money is riding on his play this season, and so far, it has fallen short, but there is still time to make headway. Last year with the Penguins, Wotherspoon finally established himself as a full-time NHLer after years as a tweener with the Boston Bruins and New York Islanders. In Pittsburgh, he formed a de facto top pairing with three-time Norris Trophy winner Erik Karlsson , who, of course, had a renaissance. That pairing was incredibly effective, making Wotherspoon’s June trade to Vegas all the more shocking. But given where the Penguins are and with the benefit of hindsight, it makes sense they moved the 29-year-old. Many folks felt Wotherspoon elevated Karlsson’s play with his defensive work, but now that Wotherspoon is struggling to gain traction in Vegas, some might wonder whether Karlsson helped elevate Wotherspoon. If you're a fisherman by trade or by hobby, you know there are times where you can see the outlines of a big fish moving just under the top of the water, just out of sight before it eventually breaches the surface and reveals itself fully. Its form provides the warning sign something is surfacing, and you can't say you didn't see it coming. In the NHL, that fish is the Carolina Hurricanes at this point in the 2026-27 regular season. At a time when many of the elite teams in the Eastern Conference have taken their big swing – the Montreal Canadiens acquired Dylan Larkin, the New Jersey Devils landed Connor Hellebuyck, the Florida Panthers acquired Brady Tkachuk back in the summer – the Hurricanes have been quietly dominating. GM Eric Tulsky's team isn't in need of any glaring upgrades at the moment, but he's in a very fortunate position with a top-tier team, tradable assets, and $10.3 million in cap space to work with. items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Recall Artur Akhtyamov By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Toronto Maple Leafs recalled netminder Artur Akhtyamov from the Toronto Marlies in the AHL. Toronto had two open roster spots, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. As of now, there is no known reason why the Maple Leafs called up Akhtyamov. Toronto has an upcoming back-to-back series in Boston and Pittsburgh, leading to speculation that the Maple Leafs might rest Sergei Bobrovsky due to his recent struggles on the ice. However, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman confirmed that Bobrovsky will start on Saturday against the Penguins. Since there aren’t any goaltending injuries to speak of, Anthony Stolarz will likely start Friday against the Bruins Still, considering they have the roster space, Toronto is likely using Akhtyamov as insurance for their upcoming back-to-back. The Maple Leafs are well aware that injuries are a constant concern. As for Akhtyamov, today’s transaction is his third call-up of the 2026-27 campaign. Unfortunately, he hasn’t appeared for Toronto yet. He’s played exclusively for the Marlies, going 3-3-3 in nine contests with an .886 SV% and 2.92 GAA. Still, it was around this time last season that Akhtyamov made his NHL debut in a loss to the Edmonton Oilers. Still, most of his season was spent with the Marlies, where he posted a 21-12-4 record with a .904 SV% and 2.88 GAA. The Maple Leafs signed him to a three-year, $2.7MM ($900K AAV) extension in March of last season.

The world juniors provides prospects with an excellent opportunity to announce themselves to the hockey world every year. Draft-eligible players can cement themselves as top prospects, and drafted prospects can compete against the world's best while representing their country at a major event. His timeline for a return from a lower-body injury was recently extended to 12 weeks. MacKinnon and Makar both left in the second period of the Avalanche’s 4-3 overtime loss in Ottawa on Nov. 12. MacKinnon went down to his knees holding his right hip after being pushed while trying to gain control of the puck. Makar left favoring his right leg. He explained Wednesday he was taking the puck up the ice when he tweaked something. “Just one of those kind of fluke things, Makar said. ”Got to let it calm down for a bit. Haven’t had it for a while." The two-time Norris Trophy winner as the NHL’s top defenseman has five goals and 18 assists in 19 games this season. He's averaging more than 22 minutes on the ice and ready to take on that kind workload. “Anytime you come back from an injury, you've got to be ready to go,” Makar said. “Regardless if I’m playing 30 (minutes), if I’m playing 15, whatever team needs me for, I’ll be there for it.” Avalanche coach Jared Bednar echoed that: “He’s cleared to play,” he said. “He's going to play.” Because of a quirk in the schedule, the Avalanche haven't played since a 4-0 win over Anaheim last Thursday. “A little bit weird,” Makar said of the prolonged break. “To be out for two weeks-ish and really miss ... three games, I’ll take it.” The team went 2-1 in his absence. items.body: Register Login Ducks Reassign Noah Warren By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 12:00 pm Yesterday afternoon, the Anaheim Ducks announced they reassigned defenseman Noah Warren to the San Diego Gulls in the AHL. The transaction drops Anaheim to 22 players on the active roster. Until yesterday, Warren had been a constant on the Ducks’ defensive corps all season. After playing two years for the Gulls, the former 42nd overall pick cracked Anaheim’s opening-night roster to begin the 2026-27 campaign. In San Diego, Warren registered two goals and 16 points in 122 games from 2024 to 2026. There’s no question the 6’5″, 216lbs defender isn’t known for his offensive skills. Still, Warren didn’t look entirely out of place with the Ducks this season, tallying six assists in 23 contests on a -3 rating while averaging 15:33 of ice time per game. Regardless of yesterday’s demotion, Warren should expect to hold down a long-term spot with the Ducks relatively soon. Anaheim lost multiple defenders this past offseason, and although he likely won’t contribute a ton offensively, Warren’s mobility, especially at his size, makes him a useful talent to have on the back end. Meanwhile, the Ducks could go multiple different directions with their newfound roster spot. Currently, Anaheim is waiting for forwards A.J. Greer and Beckett Sennecke to return from injury. items.title: Babcock explains decision not to challenge possible Oilers goal vs. Vegas
items.summary: Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3.
items.body: Already down 2-0 early to the Vegas Golden Knights , the Edmonton Oilers got a puck past Carter Hart in the first period on Tuesday, but the play was ruled no-goal. The reason? Officials determined Oilers forward Mathieu Joseph had interfered with Hart on the play while battling for position with Vegas defenceman Rasmus Andersson . That left the Oilers with a choice. Do they challenge the ruling and try to cut the deficit in half or let the game play on? Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3. "Our guy went in on his own and then he bumped their stick," Babcock said after the game when asked about not challenging. "I haven't been back very long, but I've just learned they don't (overturn) anything. So unless you're 100 per cent sure, why be shorthanded?" Joseph said he didn't feel contact with Hart in the heat of the battle but conceded it was risky to challenge at that stage of the game. "It was a pretty tough call," Joseph said. "I was just trying to get in there. I feel like I'm getting pushed back a little bit ... Sometimes the bounces don't go your way, but you've got to stick with it."

When Stan Wong isn't tending to injured hockey players as a head athletic trainer, he's working at the Oriental Chow Mein Company, a Massachusetts business his family established after they immigrated from China more than a century ago. "Whether I'm a chow mein maker or an athletic trainer, I strive to be the best I can be, and I don't take that lightly," Wong said. "That's how much I push myself. That's what I expect." For more than 40 years, Wong given his best as a beloved head athletic trainer with the Washington Capitals (1986-99) and Florida Panthers (1999-2002), and for 59 United States teams in international competitions from world championships to the Winter Olympics. Wong's dedication to players, his professionalism and infectious personality are why the 68-year-old from Fall River, Massachusetts, is being inducted into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 30 in Washington, D.C. items.title: Oilers show natural signs of fatigue in loss to Vegas after taxing road trip
items.summary: The Oilers looked tired, performed tired, and made tired mistakes in a loss to the Golden Knights on Tuesday, It’s just not easy for a team to be at its best after a six-game Eastern road swing.
items.body: EDMONTON — A hockey player will never just come out and say it. Maybe it’s because a hockey fan who goes to work for far longer hours for waaaay less pay simply doesn’t want to hear it. The Edmonton Oilers looked tired, performed tired, and made tired mistakes in their 5-3 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday, and for the first time in the Mike Babcock era a four-game losing streak has darkened the Oilers’ door. The Oilers are bushed, coming off a six-game Eastern swing with two back-to-backs, and a disciplined Vegas team smartly took advantage of the Oilers’ state. “I didn’t think we were very good with the puck,” began Connor McDavid, who was by his standards below average on Tuesday. “It’s been a tough stretch, obviously. A lot of games, a lot of travel, a lot of late nights. There’s no excuse.” The Oilers beat the Florida Panthers exactly a week before in Sunrise, outplaying a Panthers team that was on the final game of a stretch of seven games in 11 days. “The brains were right. The hands and the legs weren’t there,” Florida head coach Paul Maurice said of his team that night. “The will was there, the heart was there … We just couldn’t get to some of the places we needed to get to.” In hockey, where players are young, fit, and fly on luxurious charters with hotel-to-hotel service, the word “tired” is not defined by sore muscles and aching backs. Tired means shlepping from town to town, from time zone to time zone, with barely any time in between to unpack. And its results show up in mental lapses like Tuesday’s, where some familiar maladies arose in a season where many of these Oilers have kicked those old habits. Remember Leon Draisaitl and that turnover at the offensive blueline? He’d mostly eliminated that from his game, until this last four-game stretch.

items.body: Register Login Brandon Hagel, Zemgus Girgensons Trending To Return Wednesday By Ryan Long | at November 24, 2026 6:58 pm The Lightning appear set to get two forwards back Wednesday. Eduardo A. Encina of the Tampa Bay Times reports that Brandon Hagel and Zemgus Girgensons are “trending in the right direction” to play against the Carolina Hurricanes, pending a few tests each still needs to pass. Hagel has missed Tampa Bay’s last three games with a lower-body injury that he suffered on November 14 in a 2-0 loss to the Red Wings. The Bolts placed the Saskatoon native on injured reserve on November 19. Before the injury, the 28-year-old winger was tied with Jake Guentzel for the team lead with 13 goals and had 24 points in 20 games. Girgensons left the November 17 win over the Capitals late in the first period after a hit from Matt Roy . He has missed the two games since with an upper-body injury. The veteran has one goal and three assists in 18 games this season. While the Latvian won’t provide the offensive jolt Hagel does, he fills the third-line center role and plays on the top penalty-kill unit. The penalty kill has been a weakness for the Lightning this season, ranking 24th in the league at 73.3 percent. Tampa Bay still needs to activate Hagel from IR, and Monday’s reassignment of Jansen Harkins to AHL Syracuse freed up the roster spot to do that. Girgensons was never placed on injured reserve, so the Lightning won’t need to make a corresponding roster move for his return. The Lightning sit second in the Atlantic Division and third in the Eastern Conference with a 15-6-2 record, and with two of their top nine forwards trending to return tomorrow, will look to improve upon their impressive start as they enter into the holiday season.

Sharks’ Celebrini on Bedard injury: ‘I feel for him’
items.summary: Macklin Celebrini is sending support to Connor Bedard after the Chicago Blackhawks captain went under the knife this week.
items.body: Macklin Celebrini is sending support to Connor Bedard after the Chicago Blackhawks captain went under the knife this week. The Blackhawks announced on Monday that Bedard would miss four months after having surgery on his left shoulder, which he injured while taking a face-off last week. The injury comes after Bedard spent most of the summer and the start of this season rehabbing an injury to his right shoulder. Celebrini and Bedard both hail from North Vancouver, B.C., and train together in the off-season. On Tuesday, Sharks beat reporter Sheng Peng asked Celebrini if he had a message for his friend as he begins another long rehab process. "Knowing how much he went through with his shoulder over the summer... it sucks and I feel for him," Celebrini said. "It's not fun rehabbing... Hopefully this is the last of it and he's healthy for the rest of his career." Bedard was scoring at a point-per-game pace before his injury, with a team-leading 18 points in just 15 games.

items.body: The New York Islanders placed winger Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve and recalled centre Calum Ritchie from the AHL's Hamilton Hammers, the NHL club announced Tuesday. Palmieri was injured during Monday's loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. He sustained a lower-body injury after getting tangled with Leafs players near the net and taking an awkward fall toward the goal. He logged 8:12 of ice time before being removed for the rest of the game. There's no timeline on Palmieri's return. He has nine points in 23 contests at the time of the injury. Despite registering 30 points in his 65-game rookie season, 2023 first-round pick Ritchie has only recorded two points in eight games of action so far this season.

items.summary: U.S. Thanksgiving has traditionally served as a measuring stick for where each NHL team's competitive outlook for the season stands. Could this year be an outlier?
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 10:56 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 10:56 PM Updated Nov 24, 2026 10:57 PM U.S. Thanksgiving has traditionally served as a measuring stick for where each NHL team's competitive outlook for the season stands. Could this year be an outlier? There are multiple checkpoints throughout each NHL season where teams assess their competitive hopes, and U.S. Thanksgiving is traditionally a very important one. Every team has just recently passed the first quarter of the regular season, and there's still a ton of hockey to be played. But as history shows, this point in the calendar typically dictates a lot of what we'll see throughout the rest of the year. So what makes U.S. Thanksgiving such an important part of the NHL calendar? Over the past five seasons, 11 of the 16 teams who qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs were in post-season positions at American Thanksgiving. Going back even further, an average of 12.28 teams in playoff spots at this benchmark since the 2005-06 season have ended up in the post-season (excluding the 2012-13 lockout, along with the shortened 2020 and 2021 seasons. That's a nearly 20-year sample size with almost 77 percent accuracy. items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Reassign Ryan Tverberg, Brendan Brisson By Brennan McClain | at November 24, 2026 4:38 pm According to a team announcement , the Toronto Maple Leafs assigned forwards Ryan Tverberg and Brendan Brisson to the Toronto Marlies in the AHL. The Maple Leafs’ active roster now stands at 21. Tverberg, 24, has been with the Maple Leafs for the past two weeks. The former seventh-round pick had an uneventful recall, going scoreless in seven contests with a -4 rating, while averaging 11:24 of ice time per game. During his call-up, Tverberg spent most of his time alongside John Tavares and William Nylander . The line combination didn’t prove fruitful, as the trio produced a 36.7% xGoals%, according to MoneyPuck . Furthermore, Toronto had lost every game with Tverberg on the roster until yesterday evening, when they defeated the New York Islanders. In his eight career appearances with the Maple Leafs, the only win he’s been a part of was against the Islanders. Meanwhile, like Tverberg, Brisson has spent much of the past two weeks with the Maple Leafs after being recalled on November 12th. Still, unlike Tverberg, he did not play. After clearing waivers before the season, Brisson can spend 18 more days with Toronto before he becomes waiver-eligible again. Although he hasn’t appeared in an NHL contest with Toronto, he’s having a good season by all accounts. In the AHL, with the Marlies, Brisson has registered eight goals and 17 points in 14 games with a -2 rating. Last season, the former first-round pick scored 19 goals and 37 points in 66 games with the Hartford Wolf Pack.

According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , the Panthers have placed Cole Schwindt on waivers. As much as it would hurt to lose two forwards in a matter of days, Florida is expected to return Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for tomorrow’s contest against the Ottawa Senators. With respect to Reinhardt and Schwindt, the Panthers would comfortably make that swap 11 out of 10 times. Like Reinhardt, Schwindt made his way to Florida via waivers. The Panthers claimed the bottom-six forward a few days before the puck dropped in the 2025-26 season. He spent the entire regular season with Florida, scoring five goals and seven points in 29 games with a +2 rating. He also displayed decent physicality by blocking 11 shots and delivering 39 hits. This year, aside from a five-game stretch with the Charlotte Checkers in the AHL, Schwindt has again featured with the Panthers. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been productive, going scoreless in 15 appearances with a -5 rating, while averaging 8:28 of ice time per game. Still, he looked good with the Checkers, registering one goal and three points. If he clears waivers, unlike Reinhardt, the Panthers will likely assign Schwindt back to Charlotte. Still, he’s signed through next season at a league minimum salary, and a forward-needy team might be interested in him.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The New York Islanders have finally provided a status for Kyle Palmieri, as the winger was placed on injured reserve earlier on Tuesday. This transaction comes in the wake of Monday’s 4-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs , where Palmieri sustained a lower-body injury in the second period after an awkward fall caused him to fall into the Islanders net. He left the game shortly after, and was announced as out for the rest of the game ahead of the third period. Palmieri’s status was unknown to start Tuesday, as even when the Islanders held a practice, no update was provided on him other than that he was seeing the doctor that day to get a proper prognosis. While the Islanders have yet to make a formal announcement of Palmieri’s timeline for return, an IR placement at least confirms that he will miss at least the next seven days with his injury, as he is not allowed to be activated off of IR within that time. The Islanders play three games within the next seven days. At this point in time, no other roster moves have been made in response to Palmieri’s IR placement. Palmieri has had a slow start to the season by his standards, as he has just four goals and five assists for nine points in 23 games . It’s the worst scoring pace of his career since establishing himself as an NHL regular in 2013, although it should be expected for a player who is now 35 years old. With Palmieri out of the lineup, Mathew Barzal is expected to replace the Smithtown, New York product on the top line alongside Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom. In the last three seasons, this trio has held the score even at 3-3 and has a 36.18% 5v5 expected goal share in 58:49 of ice time, according to Natural Stat Trick . Mitchell Chaffee is expected to draw into the lineup in place of Palmieri.

items.body: Register Login Wild Place Calvin Pickard On Waivers By Gabriel Foley | at November 24, 2026 1:27 pm Following Filip Gustavsson ’s season debut on Monday, the Minnesota Wild have placed third-string goaltender Calvin Pickard on waivers. This will solidify Minnesota’s goaltending duo after Gustavsson recovered from his offseason hip surgery. Pickard appeared in three games while serving as backup to Jesper Wallstedt through the start of the season. He set a 1-1-1 record with a .855 save percentage and 3.60 goals-against-average. Minnesota signed Pickard to a one-year, $1MM contract over the summer. That deal will maintain his $1MM salary through an assignment to the minor-leagues – a small perk for the veteran of 15 pro seasons. Across his career, Pickard has recorded a 161-117-40 record and .913 save percentage in 329 AHL games. He has also set a 75-78-15 record and .900 save percentage in 194 NHL games. Now 34 years old, he brings the leadership of a seasoned pro to Minnesota’s depth chart. A seven-figure salary will likely prevent any teams from claiming Pickard, setting him up for a second-straight season of AHL minutes. Pickard could take over an Iowa Wild crease that has been split between Riley Mercer and William Rousseau . The two have nearly identical stat lines – with Mercer setting a 3-5-2 record and .900 save percentage in 10 games while Rousseau has a 3-5-1 record and .899 save percentage in nine games. Notably, Rousseau is on an AHL contract, which could make him the most expendable option in a room with two other goalies on NHL deals. Rousseau could even be a candidate for a move to the ECHL, though it’ll be to a new team after the Iowa Heartlanders folded over the summer. Minnesota is now affiliated with the Jacksonville Icemen.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Edmonton Oilers announced that forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins will return to the lineup to face the Vegas Golden Knights in their game Tuesday night. He is expected to be on a line with Connor McDavid and Kasperi Kapanen . Nugent-Hopkins missed the last five games and has been out of the lineup since the Oilers’ 1-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs Nov. 14. The 33-year-old center has four goals and seven assists for 11 points in 12 games this season. Now in his 16th season, Nugent-Hopkins has 295 goals and 520 assists for 815 points in 1,043 regular-season games. Last January, he played his 1,000th career game . He’s also played in 102 career playoff games, where he’s scored 25 goals and recorded 61 assists for 86 points. He was part of Edmonton’s back-to-back Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025. Nugent-Hopkins, a native of Burnaby, B.C., hit career highs in all offensive categories in 2022-23 when he recorded 37 goals and 67 assists for 104 points. He’s recorded at least 50 points in nine seasons. Taken with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, Nugent-Hopkins spent two full seasons with the WHL’s Red Deer Rebels, where he scored 55 goals and recorded 116 assists for 166 points in 136 regular-season games. In his draft season, he recorded 31 goals and 75 assists for 106 points in 69 games. Internationally, he represented Canada at the 2013 World Junior Championship, where he scored four goals and 11 assists for 15 points. He also played for Team North America at the 2016 World Cup of Hockey, where he scored a goal and two assists for three points.

items.body: A singer and former Broadway actress issued an emotional apology to Canadians after fumbling the lyrics to O Canada ahead of Monday night's matchup between the Toronto Maple Leafs and New York Islanders . Sarrah Strimel Bentley sang "We lend our hearts to thee" several times in place of "We stand on guard for thee." She also replaced "in" with "with" when she sang "True patriot love with all of us command." The singer took to social media shortly after to apologize and ask people to "be kind and show grace." Strimel Bentley said in an Instagram video that due to breast cancer she experiences menopause, which can be induced early by cancer treatments and can cause lapses in memory. She said she also experienced nerves singing an unfamiliar anthem in front of an audience of thousands. “I just wish that you would be a little easier on someone who is just a human being, and I'm sorry," Strimel Bentley said through tears. "Thank you for giving me grace. I love Canada. I stand on guard for thee." The Leafs referenced the lyric mishap in a post on X that shared video of defenceman Jack McCabe putting a puck in the Islanders' net for Toronto's first goal of the night. They would go on to beat the Islanders 4-2, ending a nine-game losing streak.

items.summary: In the midst of the second season under the CHL and NCAA's eligibility changes, WHL commissioner Dan Near is still pleased with where the league stands as a developmental ground for the next generation of NHL stars.
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 3:29 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 3:29 PM In the midst of the second season under the CHL and NCAA's eligibility changes, WHL commissioner Dan Near is still pleased with where the league stands as a developmental ground for the next generation of NHL stars. The NCAA's new eligibility rule has changed junior hockey in North America. The 2026-27 season is the second under the new rule, which now allows CHL players to play for colleges in the United States. Players have taken full advantage of this, as over 400 players who have suited up in either the WHL, OHL or QMJHL are currently playing Division I hockey. While teams across the CHL are losing high-end players earlier than expected, the new NCAA eligibility rule has positively affected recruitment. Players who had previously committed to the NCAA can now join CHL teams instead of playing in leagues such as the BCHL, AJHL or USHL. Even if these players are only in the league for one or two seasons, having access to this talent pool is something that excites WHL Commissioner Dan Near. "The influx of players in the Western League since the NCAA rule change has been pretty substantial as far as the number coming in versus the number going out," said Near in Chilliwack, B.C., on Monday. "I would say it's harder to play in the league than it ever has been before." items.body: Register Login Canadiens Recall Brett Berard, David Reinbacher By Gabriel Foley | at November 24, 2026 8:34 am The Montreal Canadiens have fortified their depth ahead of a three-game road trip through the Western Conference. Montreal recalled winger Brett Berard and defenseman David Reinbacher . The two will serve as the only extra skaters on a Canadiens roster facing multiple injuries. Forwards Josh Anderson , Chris Kreider , and Ivan Demidov are all on injured reserve, while defenseman Mike Matheson is also sidelined. None of the four injured players will join Montreal’s upcoming travel. Both Berard and Reinbacher have been a part of Montreal’s response to so many injuries. Berard played in his first three games with Montreal last week. He recorded one assist and two shots on goal across those appearances, before returning to the Laval Rocket for one game this weekend. Reinbacher made an appearance in the Canadiens’ lineup on Saturday and recorded a plus-two before also being reassigned for Laval’s Sunday matchup. Across the AHL season, Berard has racked up a productive 11 points in 18 games. He is one of many cylinders firing in the Laval offense, improving on a dip in minor-league scoring through his final two years in the New York Rangers’ organization. Berard scored 48 points in 71 games of his rookie AHL season but followed that with 45 points in 71 games across the next two years. Through those appearances, he also played in 48 games with the Rangers, marked by 10 points, 14 penalty minutes, and a minus-seven. Reinbacher has a tamer seven points, plus-eight, and 22 penalty minutes in 16 AHL games this season. The former fifth-overall pick continues to serve as a focal point of the Rockets’ lineup, while notching his second season with a pair of NHL appearances.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Calgary Flames center Morgan Frost left Monday’s game against the Ottawa Senators during the second period after sustaining an upper-body injury. Frost, 27, was visibly shaken up after taking a hard hit from Senators defenseman Tyler Kleven early in the middle frame. After heading down the tunnel toward the Flames’ dressing room, Frost briefly returned and played a couple more shifts before leaving the game for good. Kleven was not penalized for the hit, but Flames winger Joel Farabee was assessed two roughing penalties for his role in the post-whistle scrum; Ottawa’s Ridly Greig was also called for roughing on the play. Frost logged 8:53 of ice time, took one shot on goal, and finished with a minus-one rating across 10 shifts before exiting Monday’s game. The Flames ultimately lost the game by a 2-1 final score. Through 25 games with the Flames this season, Frost has collected five goals and 14 points. The Aurora, Ont. product is under contract with the Flames at a $4.375 million contract through the end of 2026-27, at which point he can become an unrestricted free agent. The Flames acquired Frost and Farabee together from the Philadelphia Flyers midway through the 2024-25 season. Frost set a new career high with 22 goals in 82 games with the Flames in 2025-26; he tied Mikael Backlund for second on the team with 43 points. The Flyers originally selected Frost in the first round (No. 27 overall) of the 2017 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ center followed up a strong junior career with the OHL’s Soo Greyhounds by turning pro within the Flyers organization in 2019-20, appearing in his first 20 NHL games with the club that year. items.body: Bylsma discusses why teams having trouble protecting late leads The Coaches Room is a regular feature throughout the 2026-27 season by former NHL coaches and assistants who turn their critical gaze to the game and explain it through the lens of a teacher. In this edition, Dan Bylsma, former coach of the Pittsburgh Penguins, Buffalo Sabres and Seattle Kraken and assistant with the New York Islanders and Detroit Red Wings, examines some of the reasons behind teams struggling to protect multigoal leads and defending against 6-on-5. So far this season, comebacks and 6-on-5 goal-scoring are more prevalent. These are two things that go together: Teams have come back from two or three goals down and, often, scored 6-on-5 to do it. The Winnipeg Jets came back after trailing by four goals twice in a span of 12 days. The Florida Panthers were the only team in NHL history to do that previously, accomplishing it twice (Nov. 12-21, 2019, and April 2-5, 2022). Winnipeg scored a 6-on-5 goal and a 6-on-4 goal in overcoming a 4-0 deficit in a 5-4 overtime win against the Montreal Canadiens on Nov. 3 and came back from 4-0 down again, with help from another 6-on-5 goal, in a 5-4 shootout victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Nov. 14. The Dallas Stars came back from two goals down in the last 1:18, scoring twice 6-on-5 before defeating the Vegas Golden Knights 4-3 in overtime on Nov. 17. The Edmonton Oilers forward is on pace to challenge the 200-point plateau, which is something only Wayne Gretzky has been able to achieve in the history of the NHL. “It’s incredible,” Gretzky said in Toronto this month. “First of all, he’s a tremendous young man. items.title: Islanders’ Kyle Palmieri leaves game with lower-body injury
items.summary: Palmieri took an awkward fall during the second period on Tuesday night against the Maple Leafs.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Not the greatest sight on Long Island. During a matchup between the New York Islanders and Toronto Maple Leafs , Islanders forward Kyle Palmieri left the game prematurely due to a lower-body injury. The veteran center was hurt several minutes into the second period. While trying to tie up Maple Leafs forward Easton Cowan, Palmieri started to lose his balance before awkwardly colliding with an also-falling Nick Paul, with Palmieri crashing into the Islanders’ net. The 35-year-old was able to return to the bench, but he eventually went down the tunnel into the Isles’ dressing room. The team confirmed once the third period began that Palmieri wouldn’t be coming back to the game. Palmieri logged a season-low 8:12 of ice time across nine shifts. The Islanders were up 2-0 on the Leafs before Palmieri’s injury. However, the Isles squandered the lead, as Toronto scored four unanswered goals to pick up the win, ending the Leafs’ nine-game losing streak. Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer didn’t have an update on Palmieri following the contest. The Smithtown, N.Y. native had appeared in each of the team’s first 23 games of the 2026-27 season. He has notched four goals and five assists for nine points, with a plus/minus of +2 while averaging 16:07 of ice time per game. Palmieri is in the second and final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in May 2025. The deal has a cap hit of $4.75 million, with a modified no-trade clause where the player submits a 16-team no-trade list. Despite the loss, the Islanders (11-7-5) remain third in the Metropolitan Division, 12 points back of the first-place Carolina Hurricanes . The Isles are back in action on Wednesday night, as they host the St. Louis Blues .

items.title: Ullmark leads Senators to win over Flames
items.summary: Linus Ullmark continued his impressive start to the season on Monday, making 34 saves to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames.
items.body: Linus Ullmark continued his impressive start to the season on Monday, making 34 saves to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames. Michael Amadio and Shane Pinto each scored, allowing Ottawa (16-6-3) to close out its three-game homestand with a 2-0-1 record. Matt Coronato scored the lone goal for the Flames (10-13-2), who were playing the first of a five-game Eastern road trip. Devin Cooley, who continues to look for his first road win of the season (0-4-0) was busy, stopping 29 of 31 shots. The Flames made it a one-goal game, 2-1, when Coronato scored a third-period power-play goal beating Ullmark glove side. The Flames found themselves short-handed early in the second after Ottawa’s Tyler Kleven caught Morgan Frost with a hard bodycheck that sent the Calgary forward to the ice. The hit was reviewed but no penalty was assessed. Joel Farabee was instead handed a double minor for roughing after coming to Frost’s defence, while Ottawa’s Ridly Greig received a roughing minor. With 48 seconds remaining in the period the Senators had a scare when Tim Stutzle hit the goalpost and grabbed his left knee. The Senators leading scorer went right to the dressing room but was back on the ice for the third. Amadio opened the scoring midway through the period when he intercepted the puck out front, made a move to pull Cooley and beat him glove side. Just over five minutes later Pinto stepped into the faceoff circle and snapped a shot past Cooley for his 10th of the season. Cooley faced a flurry of shots in the early parts of the period and made four straight saves to keep the Senators at bay. With Monday’s win the Senators matched their longest point streak, nine games (7-0-2), since a run in 2014-15.

Between-the-legs finish from Alex Laferriere! 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/rmz6IGtcvR Coming off a power play face-off, Laferriere played the puck off the end board after a shot from teammate Quinton Byfield went wide. Laferriere corralled the puck between his legs and pushed it passed Canadiens goalie Jakub Dobes for the score.

items.title: Gavin McKenna scores as the Maple Leafs beat the Islanders to end their 9-game skid
items.summary: — Gavin McKenna scored the go-ahead goal on a delayed penalty with just over 11 minutes remaining, and the Toronto Maple Leafs ended their losing streak at nine games by rallying to defeat the New York Islanders 4-2 on Monday night.

items.title: Bedard out four months for Blackhawks following shoulder surgery
items.summary: Connor Bedard had successful surgery on his right shoulder Monday, and the Chicago Blackhawks captain is expected to make a full recovery in approximately four months, Blackhawks team physician Dr. Michael Terry said in a statement.
items.body: Captain was injured during face-off against Maple Leafs on Nov. 17 Connor Bedard had successful surgery on his right shoulder Monday, and the Chicago Blackhawks captain is expected to make a full recovery in approximately four months, Blackhawks team physician Dr. Michael Terry said in a statement. The 21-year-old center was injured in the Blackhawks’ 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Nov. 17. He was set to take a face-off against Maple Leafs forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when, as Bedard put his stick on the ice, Paul’s stick made contact with Bedard’s right hand. The Blackhawks captain yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. Bedard has 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games this season, tied for the Blackhawks lead with forward Roman Kantserov (13 goals, five assists). Bedard scored his seventh goal of the season at 18:51 of the second period on Tuesday, giving the Blackhawks a 3-2 lead. “Obviously we’re thinking about him,” forward Patrick Kane said Thursday. “I think he knows how big of a piece he is to this team, what he means to the organization. Entertainment value, right, for fans and for the League and what he’s able to provide to the game. So, obviously it’s tough when you’re missing a player like that. “But yeah, just let him know we’re here for him. I’m not sure what the extent of it is and what’s going to happen down the road, but hopefully we can pick him up while he’s out.” It’s the third shoulder injury for Bedard in less than a year. He injured his left shoulder during an offseason training session in Vancouver on July 2 and had surgery a few days later. items.title: McKenna helps Maple Leafs beat Islanders to end winless streak
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs spotted the New York Islanders a 2-0 lead on Monday and it appeared as if the Canadian visitors were on their way to a 10th straight loss. But Dakota Joshua, Chris Tanev, Gavin McKenna and Easton Cowan with an empty-netter, scored four unanswered goals for the Leafs, who beat the Islanders 3-2 to win their first game in November and halt a losing skid that started after beating the lowly Vancouver Canucks 4-2 on Oct. 31. Anthony Duclair and Mathew Barzal scored for the Islanders, who had won four of their last five heading into the game at UBS Arena. Matthew Kessel found a wide open Anthony Duclair in the slot, who scored his seventh of the season at 3:12 of the first period to give the Islanders a 1-0 lead. Mathew Barzal made it 2-0 at 6:55 of the second period firing a snap shot past the screened Anthony Stolarz. It was Kessel's second assist of the game. Dakota Joshua of the Leafs scored at 10:14 of the second period to reduce the deficit to 2-1, then defenceman Chris Tanev tied the game 2-2 at 3:52 of the third period. McKenna put the Leafs ahead to stay with a goal at 8:55 of the third. Unlike previous games during their losing streak, the Leafs did not blow the lead. And Cowan sealed the deal with an empty-netter at 18:07 of the third. Stolarz stopped 19 of 21 shots for the Leafs, while Ilya Sorokin stopped 29 of 32 shots in the Islanders' net. The Islanders lost veteran winger Kyle Palmieri to an apparent right leg injury.
